Signage for Jio Platforms Ltd. ahead of the company's listing ceremony at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in Mumbai, India, on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images Jio Platforms' shares rose 21.4% on their trading debut Wednesday after a record initial public offering that was lapped up by retail as well as institutional investors. India's largest telecom and digital services player had offered 270 million shares in the IPO priced at 1,119 rupees apiece, raising 302 billion rupees ($3.2 billion) in the country's largest-ever IPO. The public issue was subscribed more than 22 times, with institutional investors leading the demand, according to data from the BSE. The qualified institutional portion was subscribed 70.55 times, while retail investors subscribed 2.72 times. The IPO was fully subscribed within 95 minutes of its opening on Oct. 21, Akash Ambani, managing director of Jio Platforms and heir of the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani, said ahead of the listing. Global brokerage Nomura on Wednesday gave Jio Platforms a buy rating, setting a target price of 1,340 rupees, implying an upside of 19.7% to its IPO price. The brokerage said in a report that Jio's capex cycle is largely over and there is expected to be a sharp improvement in the company's free cash flow. Shares were last trading at 1,357 rupees. Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's flagship company, Reliance Industries , owns more than a 66% stake in Jio Platforms, followed by Meta Platforms ' affiliate Jaadhu Holdings that owns nearly 10% and Google International, which owns 7.7%, as per LSEG data. Leading global funds such as BlackRock, Capital Group and GIC participated in Jio's anchor book portion of the total fundraise, which is set aside for large institutional investors before the IPO opens for public bidding. headlines.title: Indian investors rush to Nvidia, SpaceX, Apple as local trading apps roll out access to U.S. stocks
headlines.summary: Major Indian brokerages are providing retail investors access to U.S. stocks at a time when the local market has been battered.
headlines.article_text: Indian investors rush to Nvidia, SpaceX, Apple as local trading apps roll out access Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Major online investment platforms are unlocking access to U.S. stocks for millions of Indian retail investors. Groww, an Indian broking platform that accounts for over 29% of India's 46 million active clients on broking channels, rolled out the U.S. stock trading feature earlier this month. NVIDIA, SpaceX, Apple, Alphabet, Amazon, Micron and Meta are the most popular stocks among retail investors. INDIA - 2026/07/22: In this photo illustration, a Spacex logo is seen displayed on a smartphone with a NYSE (New York Stock Exchange) logo in the background. Sopa Images | Lightrocket | Getty Images Major Indian online investment platforms are unlocking access to U.S. stocks for millions of retail investors eager to diversify into global assets as the country's markets continue to underperform. Earlier, access to U.S. markets and exchange-traded funds was limited to wealthier Indians, via global banks and wealth management firms. Groww, an Indian investment platform that accounts for more than 29% of the country's 46 million active investors across stock brokerages, rolled out the U.S. equity trading feature earlier this month, Harsh Jain, chief operating officer and co-founder of the company, told CNBC. NVIDIA, SpaceX , Apple , Alphabet, Amazon , Micron and Meta are the most popular companies among early users, Jain said, whose firm has provided access to more than 10,000 U.S. stocks, exchange-traded funds and fractional share ownership. Zerodha, the second-largest trading platform with a 15% share of active clients as per NSE data, has also started beta testing access to U.S. stocks and plans to launch in a few weeks, the company told CNBC. Another popular brokerage with 6.7 million active retail clients, Angel One, is also reportedly planning to launch U.S. stock trading on its platform. There is a "big interest" among Indians to invest in U.S. stocks, especially in tech companies, Nitin Jain, chief executive and director at Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Singapore, told CNBC. He added that "retail investors like whatever goes up," pointing to the frenzy among Indian investors for investing in crypto a few years back. U.S. stocks in demand "There has always been latent demand in India for investing in global companies," Somnath Mukherjee, vice president of corporate development at Zerodha, told CNBC. He said that the underperformance of the Indian stock market over the past few years and the lack of local artificial intelligence champions is driving the demand for U.S offerings. The depreciation of the Indian rupee against the dollar is also pushing investors "to keep a part of their portfolio in another currency," Mukherjee said. India's benchmark stock index, the Nifty 50, has dropped nearly 13% since the start of the year while the S&P 500 has gained over 12%. Foreign investors are fleeing the country's markets, with a record $32.5 billion in outflows in direct equities since January, as per data from Indian depository NSDL, pressuring the stock market. With the absence of any major AI company and relatively expensive valuations, investors have picked markets such as South Korea and Taiwan over India, experts said. In August, resident Indians sent over $321 million overseas for investing in equity and debt , up 111% from a year ago, according to the Indian central bank's data. In the financial year ended March 2026, outward remittances for investments in equity and debt stood at $2.6 billion. While the retail outflows are a small fraction of India's currency reserves, the worry is that they rise exactly when the rupee is weak, and US markets look strong, and thereby "amplify pressure at the worst moment," Tanvi Kanchan, associate director, head of international business and strategy, Anand Rathi Shares & Stock Brokers said. Investment now accounts for about 11.7% of total outward remittances, up from 5.8% a year ago, so Indians are shifting from spending abroad to investing abroad, Kanchan said. The exit of foreign investors and rising energy bills due to the Iran war have already hit the Indian currency , warranting the central bank to step in. Kotak's Jain cautioned that as participation increases, the Indian regulator could have "second thoughts" around allowing retail access to U.S. markets.
